objective: Optimize exact FHERMA polynomial multiplication at N65536 W1747 and N32768 W868
hardware: AWS g7e.2xlarge, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition SM120; 4 physical CPU cores; CUDA 12.8

sources.title: Cheddar
sources.read_status: Read arithmetic and NTT design sections 3.1-4.2
sources.technique: 32-bit fields, lazy modular corrections, register stages and tiled transforms
sources.application_or_limit: v103: lazy middle kernel 63.616 to 54.560 us under NCU; no repeatable complete-call gain. v104: narrower high blocks correct but nearly neutral.

sources.title: Neo (ISCA 2025)
sources.read_status: Read publisher text on matrix reformulation, base conversion and radix-16 NTT
sources.technique: Tensor cores can accelerate suitably reformulated arithmetic
sources.application_or_limit: Existing INT8 tensor conversion is relevant. FP64 tensor-core and batched A100 results do not directly transfer to SM120 single-call latency.

sources.title: TensorFHE
sources.read_status: Read selected NTT and tensor-core sections, not the entire paper
sources.technique: Digit decomposition and batched tensor-core arithmetic
sources.application_or_limit: Existing exact unsigned INT8 conversion and reconstruction already use this broad technique; no claimed additional implementation from this reading.

sources.title: Improved NTT with Tensor Cores (2026), author implementation
sources.read_status: Read README and modular arithmetic implementation; paper DOI full text was unavailable
sources.technique: Specialized 64-bit Montgomery-friendly moduli and byte-digit dot products
sources.application_or_limit: Not a drop-in change for the present 31-bit field family. Needs a separately proven and benchmarked redesign.

sources.title: Chameleon
sources.read_status: Read GPU NTT optimization sections V-A and V-B
sources.technique: Butterfly decomposition, register aggregation, coefficient shuffling and fusion
sources.application_or_limit: Register stages and shuffles already present. Used actual occupancy evidence to test narrower high-stage CTAs; end-to-end benefit was too small to select.

sources.title: cuPQC 0.6 NTT
sources.read_status: Read release and device NTT feature documentation
sources.technique: Device-side and staged NTT interfaces
sources.application_or_limit: External SDK 0.6 wrapper attempted. Monolithic nvlink crashed; isolated wrapper failed on undefined twiddle helper references and a linker internal error. No correctness or speed claim.

sources.title: The Modern CUDA Toolbox in Practice
sources.read_status: Read optimization walkthrough
sources.technique: Pinned transfers, explicit streams and measured overlap
sources.application_or_limit: v097 merged A/B transfers; v099 separated output compute chains from ordered DMA; v101 combined both, yielding repeatable complete-call improvements.

sources.title: CUDA C++ Best Practices Guide
sources.read_status: Read host/device transfer and overlap guidance
sources.technique: Batch small copies, use pinned staging, account for registration costs
sources.application_or_limit: Direct output registration was too expensive; mapped direct GPU output v102 was slower. Kept staging and ordered DMA.

sources.title: VROOM (USENIX Security 2026)
sources.read_status: Read abstract and metadata; downloaded checksum-verified v6.0.0 author artifact and read GPU README, Montgomery reductions, correction epilogue, and warp-accumulation implementation excerpts. Full paper PDF remained inaccessible.
sources.technique: General-modulus RNS arithmetic across CPU/GPU
sources.application_or_limit: Author code uses subtractive Montgomery arithmetic and explicitly bounded redundant ranges, consistent with techniques already tested here. The artifact documents a floor-versus-ceiling conversion correction; our independent integer CRT and Shoup checks remain required. No new implementation was copied.

sources.title: MIT Han Lab ncu-report-skill
sources.read_status: Read skill and relevant references; ran analysis helpers on three fresh full reports
sources.technique: Collect full metrics, per-line stalls and timelines before choosing changes
sources.application_or_limit: Applied. High-stage root accesses wasted sectors; v107 repacked twiddles by stage and column. SM120 and NCU 2026.1 metrics were used instead of assuming B200/NCU 2026.3.

sources.title: MIT Han Lab KernelWiki
sources.read_status: Reviewed skill scope
sources.technique: Architecture-specific CUDA knowledge
sources.application_or_limit: Reviewed, not applied wholesale: SM100/SM90 instructions and tuning do not automatically apply to SM120.

sources.title: K-Dense optimize-for-gpu
sources.read_status: Reviewed skill scope
sources.technique: Python and GPU application profiling
sources.application_or_limit: Not selected for this raw CUDA/C++ kernel; no global skill install.

sources.title: Nsight Systems User Guide
sources.read_status: Read graph tracing and overhead documentation
sources.technique: Node traces expose copy/compute dependencies but perturb runtime
sources.application_or_limit: Applied to v108. Node trace shows about 34 us per input DMA strip. v109 caller participation in packing passed exactness but slowed the complete main call to about 1.43 ms versus 1.13 ms control; rejected.

sources.title: CUDA graph event record and wait nodes
sources.read_status: Read native graph event dependency semantics
sources.technique: Replace per-call CPU event API submissions with recorded graph dependencies
sources.application_or_limit: v118 correctly records last input streams and waits in the tail graph; no reliable whole-call gain.

sources.title: CUDA stream memory operation ordering
sources.read_status: Read stream memory-write barrier and dependency semantics
sources.technique: CUDA-visible graph dependencies plus mapped host completion flags
sources.application_or_limit: v116 preserves D2H-before-flag ordering but is slower than the existing CUDA event approach.

sources.title: NVIDIA Heterogeneous Memory Management
sources.read_status: Read allocator, accessibility and page-placement sections
sources.technique: Direct GPU access to ordinary system allocations when supported
sources.application_or_limit: Official target reports pageable_memory_access=0, so this shortcut is unavailable. Local laptop reports 1; that local capability must not be assumed on the runner.

sources.title: WarpDrive (HPCA 2025)
sources.read_status: Read introduction and design sections IV-A through IV-C, including warp-level decomposition, register layouts, and concurrent CUDA/Tensor work
sources.technique: Small transform decomposition, byte-exact tensor products, and complementary execution pipelines
sources.application_or_limit: v125 implements an independently derived exact 16-by-32 middle transform. A direct modular DFT cross-check and 48 local plus 48 AWS oracle cases pass. Its isolated middle kernel is 108.480 us versus 63.616 us for the prior scalar kernel, and whole-call latency regresses. v126 tests disjoint concurrent CUDA/Tensor row ranges; no paper speedup is assumed transferable.

sources.title: NVIDIA CUDA graph scheduling and repeat-launch improvements
sources.read_status: Read definitions, measured launch behavior, and scheduling based on node creation order
sources.technique: Node creation order influences scheduling; straight-line kernel results do not imply constant cost for mixed memcpy/memop graphs
sources.application_or_limit: v120 ordered native-memory-wait input graph is correct but substantially slower. v126 creates the tensor branch before the independent CUDA branch. Dependencies remain explicit.

sources.title: Exact-workload discussion on NVIDIA forums
sources.read_status: Read both author posts; no expert replies were present
sources.technique: Author measurements of pinned staging, parallel packing, registration, and output allocation on the same workload
sources.application_or_limit: Registration overhead supports avoiding per-call host registration. These are participant observations, not NVIDIA validation or a newly discovered optimization.

sources.title: NVIDIA nvbandwidth
sources.read_status: Read build and usage documentation; inspected CMake; built commit 82fc4e8c6afa0babb8687793678f615b3b8d793e
sources.technique: Separate copy-engine and SM measurements at multiple transfer sizes
sources.application_or_limit: AWS tests at 1, 2, 14, 28 and 64 MiB verify data and show CE faster than SM copies. Official unscored graph-copy diagnostic confirms roughly 56 GB/s H2D and 57 GB/s D2H. These are bandwidth measurements, not ranked multiplication scores.

sources.title: Ozaki 2.5 (September 2026)
sources.read_status: Read conversion cost discussion, software reuse modes O1/O2 and the boundary between models and measured implementations
sources.technique: Keep byte/traffic accounting separate from arithmetic; fused conversion can repeat reads unless reuse is explicit
sources.application_or_limit: The target is FP64-emulated GEMM on different hardware, and several numbers are modeled projections. No projected speedup is used here. v127 explicitly loads raw coefficients once per block before processing every RNS field.

sources.title: cuPQC NTT 0.6 usage and SDK examples
sources.read_status: Read runtime modulus support, descriptor setup, standard and staged execution, and the SDK standard NTT example
sources.technique: Composable NTT device routines with Montgomery representation and precomputed twiddles
sources.application_or_limit: Downloaded the SDK on the authorized AWS instance for inspection; no cuPQC-NTT integration or measured speedup is claimed.

sources.title: Faster arithmetic for number-theoretic transforms, David Harvey
sources.read_status: Read sections2-4, including bounds and modified butterflies
sources.technique: Skip reduction of difference before Shoup when a+p-b<2^32
sources.application_or_limit: Implemented in v131 with independent bounds and polynomial checks; broader30bit lazy representation had already failed full-call selection.

sources.title: On Modular Algorithms and Butterfly Operations in Number Theoretic Transform
sources.read_status: Read sections2.2 and2.3 on signed Montgomery, Plantard, and butterfly bounds
sources.technique: Review exact operand bounds before adopting modular shortcuts
sources.application_or_limit: No Plantard implementation copied; use independent integer oracle for widened operands.

sources.title: FHERMA organizer transfer discussion, refreshed 2026-11-10
sources.read_status: Read organizer replies and input allocation guidance
sources.technique: Pinned staging, chunking and registration are in scope within fherma_run; input allocations are fresh
sources.application_or_limit: No harness allocator changes or assumptions about persistent operand addresses. Direct per-call pin/unpin measured too costly on AWS.

sources.title: fhe-ntt kernel card
sources.read_status: Read method, measurements and exactness sections
sources.technique: 64-bit Shoup with stage-wise launches over pre-existing RNS inputs
sources.application_or_limit: Its n4096/n8192 batch throughput omits wide-integer conversion and PCIe staging; not evidence of a faster complete FHERMA call. No code imported.

sources.title: FHERMA ranking and between-call idle discussion
sources.read_status: Read current visible replies, including organizer request for implementation details
sources.technique: Competitors report slower first transfers after idle gaps
sources.application_or_limit: Possible explanation of standalone versus warmed diagnostic gap. Their measurements are not our measurements; no causal claim or keep-warm implementation.

sources.read_status: Search excerpt only; direct PDF returned403
sources.application_or_limit: Uncore scaling is a hypothesis for host/transfer idle sensitivity, not an established cause or a recommendation to modify runner settings.

evidence_boundary: All candidate timings in this research record are development measurements. Only a separate official run can establish leaderboard performance. Inaccessible papers are explicitly marked.
remaining_priorities: Test host worker wait method under controlled idle, with compact logs retaining all measured cases.
Measure v150 operand pipeline against beginning and ending baseline brackets.
Keep investigating output-copy gaps; direct mapped-host final stores and grouped output DMA have already lost in target proxy measurements.

post_submission_experiments.outcome: Exact, but main latency about 1.43 ms versus 1.13 ms control; rejected.
Standard reserve/insert avoids zeroing but loses parallel output overlap; main about 1.735 ms, rejected.
138 local exact cases and repeated AWS exact checks. Main about 1.145 ms, slightly slower. Extra central high-stage kernels measured about 34 and 21 us.
Eight row chunks improve small point to about 0.353 ms but slow main to about 1.197 ms; not submitted.
Eight column strips improve small point to about 0.344 ms but slow main to about 1.188 ms. Retained as a possible size-specific follow-up, not submitted.

48 local exact checks and AWS exact checks. Small-point AWS latency improved to about 0.349 ms, but the later official-hardware diagnostic measured main inner latency about 1.139 ms versus baseline 1.035-1.041 ms. Rejected for the ranked main point.
48 local exact checks, but main about 34 ms and small about 4 ms. Repeated host-memory reads severely regress; rejected.
138 local exact checks. Native graph memory writes replace output CUDA event synchronization but main about 1.154 ms versus 1.127 ms control; rejected.
48 local exact checks plus four CUDA12.8 AWS variants. No repeatable main gain across 0/25/50/100 preferences; controls drifted from 1.153 to 1.192 ms. Not selected.
138 local exact checks and 96 candidate AWS exact checks. Main 1.121-1.126 ms, bracketed controls 1.119-1.129 ms; small 0.379-0.383 ms versus 0.371-0.372 ms. No reliable gain; rejected.

Unscored platform run passed 3/3 exact cases on 12 physical / 24 logical cores. Inner medians about 1.035 ms at 8 workers, 1.036 at 10, 1.040 at 6, 1.106 at 4, and 1.304 at 3. No substantial gain from worker-count changes; keep 8.

post_submission_experiments.candidate: v119 carry-aware lazy reduction in 31-bit fields
post_submission_experiments.outcome: 312000 independent integer arithmetic checks and 138 local exact cases; two AWS passes checked 96 cases. Retains the same 114 fields, unlike the prior 30-bit lazy variant. Main 1.117-1.126 ms versus controls 1.119-1.121 ms; no reliable full-call gain, not selected.

Unscored platform run passed 3/3 exact cases. Inner medians: baseline 1.035-1.041 ms, 64 columns 1.057 ms, 128 columns 1.159 ms, SM input copy 1.139 ms. All alternatives slower on target; no ranked submission.

Unscored platform run passed 3/3 exact cases. GPU node 0 and allowed CPUs 0-23 share the only visible NUMA node. Input/output physical-node queries were denied with EPERM. Pageable-memory access and native host atomics both report 0. No exposed NUMA-placement fix or HMM direct-input path identified.

official_idle_diagnostic.finding: A 20ms idle interval increases tuned inner median from 1.018680 to 1.336714ms; wide variability, mechanism unproven. 3/3 exact.
official_idle_diagnostic.next: Timed startup transfer size sweep with CPU and external-event CUDA graph timing.

startup_transfer_diagnostic.finding: 3/3 exact; log tail preserves only final measured case completely. Long idle slows input/CPU/output phases, middle near64us. Larger startup DMA does not consistently restore warm performance.
startup_transfer_diagnostic.caveat: Instrumented and input-reused, not standalone scores. Input-start-to-middle is robust; strip15 need not be the last input to finish.

new_operand_pipeline.change: Separate forward-A from B-forward/product/inverse; upload A first to overlap its central transform with B upload, preserving input DMA size

official_worker_idle_diagnostic.finding: 3/3 exact, all162 inner samples retained. Operand pipeline ~1.02ms vs1.037ms warm brackets. Polling alone does not fix idle; tuned polling has9delayed samples without>1.2ms but no paired tuned-wait control.
official_worker_idle_diagnostic.decision: Do not promote CPU polling as an established fix; preserve early operand overlap as a small measured lead.
